note: Hand-written by sujitn on 2026-08-07 to exercise the Reader seam (EVAL-3, ADR-0061 decision 6). The blocks are written in the renderer's own vocabulary (crates/synveda-retrieval/src/compose.rs) — scope headings, one line per entry, legend, watermark — but they came from this file, not from /v1/inject. So nothing here is a QA accuracy or a measurement of Synveda; it measures the reader and the judge. Seven probes chosen so the extractive default and a model reader must diverge: three the selector cannot do (synthesis, paraphrase, supersession) and two lures it should fall for (a lexical match that answers a different question, and a fact the model knows but the block does not hold).

probes.name: direct-line
probes.question: How many attempts are payments retries capped at?
probes.block:
## acme (org)
- [decision] Payments retries are capped at three attempts.
- [fact] The on-call rota is public.

Summarised entries end with a recall handle; `synveda recall <id>` fetches the full text.

<!-- synveda:watermark v1 blake3=aa01 records=r1,r2 -->
probes.note: both readers should get this; a set where every probe separates them would not notice a reader that had stopped working

probes.name: synthesis-across-entries
probes.question: How long did the kitchen renovation take?
probes.block:
## alice (user)
- [episode] The kitchen renovation started on 3 March.
- [episode] The kitchen renovation was signed off on 24 March.

<!-- synveda:watermark v1 blake3=aa02 records=r3,r4 -->
probes.note: 24 March minus 3 March is three weeks; neither line says it, so a reader that selects a line cannot answer and a reader that reads can

probes.name: paraphrased-question
probes.question: How do we handle unsuccessful charge reattempts?
probes.block:
## acme (org)
- [decision] Payments retries are capped at three attempts.

<!-- synveda:watermark v1 blake3=aa03 records=r1 -->
probes.note: the question shares no content word with the entry, so selection abstains where a model reads it — EVAL-4's `semantic` case, on the reading side

probes.name: supersession
probes.question: Which replica does the reconciliation job run against?
probes.block:
## acme (org)
- [decision] The payment reconciliation job runs against the ledger-archive replica.
- [decision] The payment reconciliation job now runs against the ledger-live replica.

<!-- synveda:watermark v1 blake3=aa04 records=r5,r6 -->
probes.note: both lines match the question equally; selection has no way to prefer the later one, which is ADR-0039's knowledge_update category as a reading problem rather than a retrieval one

probes.name: abstain-on-silence
probes.question: Which vendor supplies the espresso beans?
probes.block:
## alice (user)
- [episode] The kitchen renovation was signed off on 24 March.
- [preference] Alice runs cargo nextest before pushing.

<!-- synveda:watermark v1 blake3=aa05 records=r4,r7 -->
probes.note: no overlap at all; both readers should decline, and a reader that does not here is inventing outright

probes.name: abstain-on-lexical-lure
probes.question: Which vendor supplies the espresso beans?
probes.block:
## alice (user)
- [fact] The espresso beans are stored in the third cupboard.

<!-- synveda:watermark v1 blake3=aa06 records=r8 -->
probes.note: the entry shares `espresso beans` with the question and answers a different question about them; selection is expected to return it, which is precisely the invention the abstention axis exists to catch

probes.name: abstain-on-world-knowledge
probes.question: How tall is the Eiffel Tower?
probes.block:
## alice (user)
- [episode] Alice's team went up the Eiffel Tower on the Paris offsite.

<!-- synveda:watermark v1 blake3=aa07 records=r9 -->
probes.note: the model knows this and the block does not hold it; answering from training rather than from the block is the failure that would put a number on Synveda's name that Synveda did not earn
